roleDefinition: A learner who can independently produce and explain small warning-clean C++20 programs using core syntax, typed values, strings, vectors, full-line parsing, functions, const references, classes, RAII, algorithms, associative containers, checked text files, debugging, dependency-free checks, Git, and clear build instructions.
evidenceSummary: The capability boundary was triangulated across current C++ teaching, compiler and standard-library references, debugger guidance, and GitHub safety material, then constrained to eight six-hour instructional Weeks.

capabilityTiers.outcome: Compile and run code, reason about typed values, repair diagnostics, validate complete input lines, make decisions, iterate, and summarize vectors safely.

Decompose multi-file behavior, use const references, protect class invariants, reason about value ownership, transform ranges, summarize keyed data, persist defensively, debug, and run dependency-free checks.
Integrate proven modern C++ competencies into a documented, verified, persistent command-line application and publish source safely.

professionalPractices: read the first relevant diagnostic before editing
validate complete input lines and ranges before state change
prefer standard-library value types and automatic lifetime
test normal, boundary, invalid, missing, and malformed cases
preserve failed input and existing files for diagnosis
document exact build and run commands
boundaries: No raw new/delete or manual ownership requirement
graduationBoundary: Write, compile, debug, verify, document, and publish small modern C++20 programs using safe value ownership and the standard library, with enough fluency for introductory practical examinations and beginner projects.
technologyDecision: MSYS2 UCRT64 GCC/GDB, VS Code, PowerShell, the C++20 standard library, Git, and GitHub provide a maintained Windows route with high practical-exam value and no paid IDE requirement.
